title: Causal ATE Mitigates Unintended Bias in Controlled Text Generation
measurement_description: The paper uses the word 'Muslim' as an example of a 'spurious correlate' to illustrate how language models can develop unintended bias, specifically in toxicity detection. It measures how its proposed method, Causal Average Treatment Effect (ATE), can mitigate this by preventing models from incorrectly associating the religious term with toxicity due to biased training data.
findings: The paper demonstrates that terms related to religious identity, like 'Muslim', can be incorrectly flagged as toxic by language models because they act as 'spurious correlates' in training data. The proposed Causal ATE method is shown to effectively reduce this unintended bias, leading to lower and more accurate toxicity scores for sentences containing such terms.
